goal: Ship the Import offer: create it at the subscribe+connect junction, let the owner accept or decline it once per location, and enqueue the Review import only on Yes — so no import runs without Import consent (D1/D9).
non_goals: No migration — the Import consent columns shipped as migrations 100+101 (#673). The one-migration-in-flight slot stays free. This is load-bearing and it is what pushed the analytics events to #679: a new event name requires extending the analytics_events.event_name CHECK (migration 097's enum), so keeping this non-goal means shipping no analytics here (deviations D7).
No reviews list, no unanswered-first sort, no per-row Generate/Regenerate — that is #678. Imported reviews surface only through the existing dashboard recentReviews feed.

No worker-side consent guard in ZernioBackfillWorker — that is #679. This ticket ships the writer and all three enqueue gates; #679 adds the fail-closed run-time chokepoint that covers hand-inserted rows.
No stored 'expired' value, no poller, no lazy write-back, no expiry notification — expiry is derived on read (spec §5.3, #670).
No feature flag and no env-vars.md entry (ADR 0015 R1). Ordering carries the rollout; backout is git revert.
No permanent import affordance in settings (spec §8, rejected at design).

No changes to the live-ingest lane. A declined location keeps receiving live-lane drafts for new reviews — that is what the reassurance line promises. The ZernioReviewIngestWorker is not touched and never consults Import consent (asserted by #679).

No typed job_outbox helper for ZERNIO_INITIAL_BACKFILL — the topic has none today and all four producers enqueue raw; minting one would turn every raw site red under ci:outbox-seam and force migrating them in this PR (invariant #2 explicit carve-out).
No rename of the zernio_initial_backfill topic or zernio_backfill_runs table (map #667, out of scope).
No change to how add-location resolves a Google place id. The consent-lineage lookup reads google_place_id and google_maps_url as they already exist; validate_place_id resolution is untouched.

No change to reactivation idempotency. reactivateLocationTransaction gets the consent conjunct and nothing else — no completed-run predicate, no in-flight dedup. Its backfill_reason reactivation runs are meant to recur after a completed initial run.

No partial unique index on job_outbox. The businesses row lock is the chosen serialization (owner decision 2026-08-06); migration 004 index precedent is recorded in the plan as the answer if a fifth producer ever appears.
user_visible_behavior: When a location reaches the subscribe+connect junction — whichever of subscription activation and Google connection lands second — an Import offer is created with a deadline 7 days after the junction, and the dashboard shows the Import offer banner for the location currently in scope.

The banner reads: 'Import your recent reviews?' / 'We can pull in your 100 most recent Google reviews from the past year so you can generate replies for them. Nothing gets posted — you choose what to reply to.' / 'This is a one-time import, available for the next 7 days. New reviews will still be handled automatically either way.' with actions 'Import my reviews' and 'No thanks'.
Clicking 'Import my reviews' records the acceptance and enqueues the Review import in one transaction; the click returns immediately and never blocks on Zernio.

After accepting, the banner shows 'Importing your reviews… this usually takes a minute', then resolves to 'Imported N reviews. They're in your reviews list.' — or 'No recent reviews found — nothing to import.' when the import stored zero, or a neutral failure message when the import job died.
Clicking 'No thanks' records the decline and the banner disappears permanently for that location. Nothing is fetched from Zernio and no import is ever enqueued.
An owner who answers after the 7-day deadline gets no write and no import — the banner is already gone, and a late request is rejected.
A request that tries to answer before any offer exists is rejected and records nothing: a row at its 'pending' default with no deadline is not an offer.

Connecting Google no longer starts an import on its own: the junction creates the offer, and the import is enqueued only by an acceptance (or resumed for a location that already accepted and whose import never completed).
A past_due → active recovery no longer re-imports for a location that declined the offer (the §5.2 bug).

Reactivating an archived location no longer imports on its own: the catch-up import runs only when that location's Import consent is 'accepted'. Declining can no longer be defeated by archiving and reactivating from the locations UI.

Re-adding a location whose archived row for the same Google place — or the same Google Maps URL, for a location whose place id was never resolved — had declined or let the offer expire does not re-offer the import; the new row inherits that decision.
Exactly one import job is created per acceptance: a reconnect while an import is still in flight does not start a second one.
invariants: Invariant #2 (transactional outbox): the acceptance write and the zernio_initial_backfill enqueue happen in ONE Postgres transaction. Raw INSERT INTO job_outbox at all four producers — the topic has no helper. The three junction/decision producers dedup against an in-flight row using OUTBOX_IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES from src/lib/shared/job-outbox-status.ts, re-spelled byte-for-byte, never parameterized. Reactivation deliberately does NOT: it enqueues with backfill_reason reactivation, which the worker does not dedup, and an in-flight check there loses accepted-but-incomplete recovery against a worker holding a stale archived_at read.
Invariant #1 (Vercel = UI only): the decision route performs Postgres writes only. No Zernio call, no LLM call, no long-running work in Next.js — the fetch is the worker's job (D9).

Invariant #8 (auth scope): every read and write is scoped by account_id and business_id; the decision route resolves its location from owner scope and never trusts a client-supplied business id. Consent lineage lookups are scoped to the same account.

Invariant #15: import-consent.ts and import-offer-view.ts take their db client as an explicit sql/tx parameter and never import @/lib/db/server. Only the route and the ingress composition roots import the singleton.

Invariant #12: the route validates, calls ONE domain function that owns the transaction, and maps the outcome. The sql.begin, the consent transition, the outbox INSERT and the analytics enqueue live in the domain module, not the handler.
Invariant #13 / ADR 0015 R1: no feature flag, no NEXT_PUBLIC_ companion, no env-vars.md entry.

An offer must EXIST before it can be answered: the guarded UPDATE requires import_offer_expires_at IS NOT NULL AND > now(). A row at migration 100's 'pending' DEFAULT with a NULL deadline is 'no offer', never an answerable one — otherwise a direct POST manufactures consent for a location that was never asked.

F3 atomic transition contract (#673 adversarial review, shared with #679): acceptance and decline UPDATE only rows that are pending AND hold a live deadline, guarded by the UPDATE's WHERE predicate rather than read-then-write. A terminal state — accepted or declined — is never overwritten by any path, including under concurrency.

One owner for the derivation: importConsentStateSql is the single place 'pending AND import_offer_expires_at <= now()' is spelled. The offer view, the decision transaction, all three enqueue gates, and (after rebase) #679's worker guard all consult it.
D9: nothing is fetched from Zernio before an acceptance is recorded. D2: the enqueued topic is zernio_initial_backfill, never generate_response — the import writes no replies.
Expiry is evaluated by Postgres now(), never a JS Date, so the timestamptz microsecond-truncation class cannot apply at the boundary.
D8 permanence: no path resurrects a declined or derived-expired offer — not re-add of an archived location, not reactivation, not a repeated junction, not a reconnect.

Every zernio_initial_backfill producer runs inside sql.begin holding SELECT … FROM businesses … FOR UPDATE. SELECT … FOR UPDATE is a no-op outside a transaction under Supabase transaction pooling, so a producer without its own transaction is unprotected, not merely slower. This lock — not a unique index — is what makes the check-then-insert in-flight dedup safe (owner decision 2026-08-06).

createImportOffer proves the junction in its own SQL: subscription_activated_at IS NOT NULL AND an active zernio_connections row must both exist before any deadline is written. Postgres GREATEST(NULL, x) returns x, so a predicate that merely combined the two timestamps would mint a pre-junction offer for a one-sided location. The deadline itself is now() + 7 days at creation — no junction anchor, no connection-history SQL.
edge_cases: Junction fires twice (reconnect, or activation after connect) → createImportOffer is idempotent: it stamps only a pending row with a NULL deadline, so the 7-day clock is never extended or restarted.

The deadline is seven days from the moment the offer is created, not from the junction. Anchoring to the junction was considered and dropped (owner, 2026-08-06): createImportOffer writes the deadline exactly once, so the anchor only ever mattered for locations whose junction-time write failed and are later repaired by the GET self-heal — a case where a later clock start only benefits the owner. Spec §2.2 reasons about months of drift and is unaffected.

Offer creation fails on the Stripe activation path (it runs outside the activation tx, best-effort) → the GET route re-attempts createImportOffer idempotently, so a transient failure delays the banner rather than permanently denying the offer.
Junction reached with subscription_activated_at NULL → no offer is created; the existing finalize-tx warn branch is unchanged.
A decision request arrives for a row that is still at its 'pending' DEFAULT with a NULL deadline → 'no offer'; nothing is written and nothing is enqueued.

Late click — the owner answers at or after the deadline → the UPDATE matches zero rows and the route returns a gone/conflict outcome with no write and no enqueue. The <= boundary is inclusive, per §5.3's predicate verbatim.
Double-click or duplicate POST of accept → the second UPDATE matches zero rows (already accepted); the route is idempotent and exactly one import is enqueued.
Two concurrent accept requests → one transition commits, exactly one zernio_initial_backfill row is created.
Accept then decline (racing tabs) → whichever transition commits first wins; the second matches zero rows. No terminal state is overwritten.
Accept, then reconnect while the import is still in flight → the in-flight outbox dedup prevents a second zernio_initial_backfill row.

Offer accepted but the import never completes (Zernio outage, worker crash) → consent stays accepted, zernio_backfill_runs.completed_at stays NULL, and §5.1 retryability is preserved. The banner shows the importing state even when imported_count is already partially positive.

The import's outbox row reaches a terminal non-completed status → the banner reports a failed import rather than spinning forever (draft-status precedent maps every terminal non-completed status to failed).

Import completes having stored zero reviews (no reviews inside the Import window) → success, not an error: 'No recent reviews found — nothing to import.' Distinguished from a not-yet-finished run by completed_at, never by imported_count's DEFAULT 0 (spec §7).

Multi-location account → the offer, the decision, and the banner are per location; the banner shows the offer for the location currently in scope, switching scope refetches, and no location's state is ever served for another.

Re-adding an archived location → the new businesses row inherits the archived sibling import_decision / _at / _expires_at. The sibling is matched by a disjunction over non-NULL keys — equal google_place_id (both non-NULL) OR equal google_maps_url (both non-NULL), never NULL to NULL in either column — scoped to the same account, most-recently-archived first with a deterministic tie-break (F3 constraint 1). The disjunction is what covers the cross-representation case in both directions.
A location whose google_place_id was never resolved (URL-mode add) → lineage still matches through google_maps_url, so a declined URL-mode place cannot be re-offered by re-adding it.
Owner never opens the dashboard → the deadline still passes; the offer derives expired and is never shown. Nothing is imported (the fail-closed direction).
A declined location keeps receiving live-lane drafts for new reviews — declining the import is not declining the product.
Reviews already ingested live are deduped by importReview's ON CONFLICT, so an accepted import after a period of live ingestion cannot duplicate rows.

Reactivation of an accepted location that already completed an initial import → the archived-period catch-up still runs. It enqueues with backfill_reason reactivation and the worker only dedups run_reason initial, so a generic completed-run gate would silently delete the feature.
A location holding one half of the junction (activated but never connected, or connected but never activated) → no offer is created, and the GET self-heal creates none either.

rollback_plan: git revert the PR (ADR 0015 R1 — no flag exists to flip). No migration rides this ticket, so there is no schema state to undo; the Import consent columns stay and revert to being written by nobody. Reverting restores the unconditional junction and reactivation enqueues, which are inert in both environments while prod and staging hold zero businesses. Order: revert, redeploy the Railway worker (ingress change), redeploy Vercel (routes + banner). Any import_decision rows written before the revert stay on the row and are re-honoured when the PR re-lands — the record is never rewritten.
observability: NO analytics events in this ticket — deferred to #679 (owner decision 2026-08-07, deviations D7). import_offer_created and import_decision_recorded both require extending the analytics_events.event_name CHECK, which needs a migration this intake's own non_goals forbids. #679 carries the migration, both names, the docs/analytics/events.md entries and the emission sites; their ratio remains the churn signal, just one ticket later.

A structured log line from the decision transaction on a rejected request, naming the rejection class (no_offer, expired, already_answered) and business_id, so 'the owner says the button did nothing' resolves to an expiry or a missing offer rather than an outage.

A structured log line at each of the three enqueue gates when consent blocks an enqueue, naming the derived consent state — the proof that declines are actually being honoured at the product paths, and the counterpart to #679's worker-side skip line.

Counter-signal for the silent failure: an accepted import whose zernio_backfill_runs row still has completed_at NULL well past the run window means the import stalled — queryable in Railway logs alongside the run row.
No new metric or Sentry event: a decline and an expiry are expected outcomes, not errors, and paging on either would page on normal use.
